_comment: Built-in editing techniques. User techniques live in KeremKit/settings/techniques.json and override these by id. 'auto' = KeremKit can apply it without manual work; 'how' says with what.

groups.motion: Camera-style motion added in the edit

techniques.name: Jump cut
techniques.what: Cut out pauses or mistakes inside one continuous shot; the image jumps slightly.
techniques.when: Talking-head videos, vlogs, tutorials - keeps pace high.
techniques.how: transcript.py + cutlist.py build (pauses from audio, retakes removed)

techniques.name: Jump-cut zoom (punch-in on cuts)
techniques.what: Alternate the framing at every jump cut (e.g. 100% / 110%) so the cut reads as a new angle instead of a glitch.
techniques.when: Any tight-cut talking head. Use 105-115%; keep eyes inside the frame.
techniques.how: cutlist.py zoom -> one Scale expression reading zoom.json

techniques.name: Emphasis punch-in
techniques.what: Quick zoom-in on a key word or line, held until the next cut.
techniques.when: Punchlines, numbers, the main claim of a sentence.
techniques.how: cutlist.py zoom --emphasis subs.json (highlighted cues) or chosen times

techniques.name: Slow push-in
techniques.what: Very slow continuous zoom (2-5%) across a shot to add life to static footage or stills.
techniques.how: Scale keyframes over the layer's duration (ease in-out)

techniques.name: Camera shake / impact
techniques.what: Short positional shake on an impact moment or beat.
techniques.when: Drops, hits, reveals. Short (4-8 frames) and small.
techniques.how: Position wiggle expression gated by time, or a learned preset

techniques.name: J-cut
techniques.what: The next shot's audio starts before its picture: we hear B while still seeing A.
techniques.when: Moving into a new speaker, scene or the voice-over; makes transitions feel natural.
techniques.how: Extend the incoming audio layer earlier (layer.set_timing inPoint) while the video keeps its cut; typical lead 0.3-1.0 s

techniques.name: L-cut
techniques.what: The previous shot's audio continues over the next picture: we see B while still hearing A.
techniques.when: Showing a reaction, screen recording or B-roll while the speaker finishes a sentence.
techniques.how: Extend the outgoing audio layer's outPoint past the video cut; typical tail 0.3-1.5 s

techniques.name: Cutaway / B-roll
techniques.what: Cover part of the main shot with related footage while the audio continues.
techniques.when: Hide jump cuts, illustrate what is said, keep attention.
techniques.how: Footage layer above the main shot for the covered range

techniques.name: Match cut
techniques.what: Cut between two shots that match in shape, movement or composition.
techniques.when: Stylish scene changes; needs footage that matches.
techniques.how: Align the matching moments; comp.sample to compare positions

techniques.name: Cut on action
techniques.what: Cut in the middle of a movement so the motion hides the edit.
techniques.how: Place the cut 2-4 frames into the movement

techniques.name: Smash cut
techniques.what: Abrupt cut from one mood/volume to a very different one for contrast or comedy.
techniques.how: Hard cut, often with a sudden audio change

techniques.name: Whip / swish transition
techniques.what: Fast directional motion blur carrying one shot into the next.
techniques.how: Library transition or preset; motion blur on; 6-10 frames

techniques.name: Speed ramp
techniques.what: Change playback speed smoothly within a shot (fast -> slow -> fast).
techniques.how: Time remapping keyframes with eased velocity; needs footage shot at a higher frame rate for slow parts

techniques.name: Montage / rhythm cut
techniques.what: Sequence of short shots cut to the music's beat.
techniques.how: Cut points on beats; markers from the music

techniques.name: Loudness normalization
techniques.what: Bring the whole mix to a target loudness so it matches the platform (YouTube/Spotify -14 LUFS, broadcast -23).
techniques.how: audio.py process --chain loudnorm (two-pass)

techniques.name: Noise reduction
techniques.what: Reduce steady background hiss, hum or room noise.
techniques.when: Home recordings, fans, AC hum. Too much makes voices robotic.
techniques.how: audio.py process --chain denoise (FFT denoiser, gentle by default)

techniques.name: High-pass filter
techniques.what: Remove rumble below ~80 Hz (desk bumps, traffic, handling noise).
techniques.how: audio.py process --chain highpass

techniques.name: De-esser
techniques.what: Tame harsh 's' and 'ş' sounds.
techniques.how: audio.py process --chain deess

techniques.name: Voice compression
techniques.what: Even out loud and quiet parts of speech so every word is clear.
techniques.how: audio.py process --chain compress

techniques.name: Presence EQ
techniques.what: Small boost around 3-5 kHz and a cut of muddiness around 250-400 Hz for clearer speech.
techniques.how: audio.py process --chain eq

techniques.name: Music ducking
techniques.what: Music drops automatically while someone speaks and comes back in the gaps.
techniques.when: Any video with music under speech.
techniques.how: audio.py duck voice music (sidechain compression) or Audio Levels keyframes from the cut list's speech regions

techniques.name: Room tone fill
techniques.what: Fill dead-silent gaps with the room's own quiet sound so cuts don't feel like holes.
techniques.when: Tight cuts with very clean silence.
techniques.how: Loop a quiet room-tone clip under the voice track

techniques.name: Micro crossfades
techniques.what: A few milliseconds of fade at every audio cut to avoid clicks.
techniques.how: Built into cutlist.py render (5 ms)

techniques.name: Breath reduction
techniques.what: Lower (not remove) loud breaths between sentences.
techniques.how: Keep breaths with a larger pad-after, then lower their level; removing them entirely sounds unnatural

techniques.name: Multi-format delivery (reframe)
techniques.what: Make 16:9, 9:16 and 1:1 versions from one edit: duplicate the comp, resize, re-place subtitles and UI in each format's safe area.
techniques.how: references/formats.md

techniques.name: Pre-render quality check
techniques.what: Check missing fonts/footage, safe areas, text spelling, audio peaks and black/frozen frames before delivering.
techniques.how: references/qc.md + qc.py on the render

techniques.name: Layer order, naming and colour labels
techniques.what: Sort layers by role, name them with standard prefixes and give each role its own label colour.
techniques.when: After every edit (automatic unless turned off).
techniques.how: references/organize.md

techniques.name: Project log
techniques.what: A short running log in the project's _keremkit folder so work can continue in a new chat.
techniques.how: SKILL.md -> Project log

techniques.name: YouTube chapters
techniques.what: Chapter list with output times from the corrected transcript.
techniques.how: references/publish.md

techniques.name: Title and description ideas
techniques.what: Title options and a description draft from the transcript.
techniques.how: references/publish.md

techniques.name: Thumbnail frame candidates
techniques.what: Pick sharp, expressive frames as thumbnail candidates, saved as images for the user.
techniques.how: qc.py thumbs

techniques.name: EDL / FCPXML export
techniques.what: Export the cut as an EDL or FCPXML timeline to finish in Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve or Final Cut.
techniques.when: When the finish happens in another editor.
techniques.how: cutlist.py export
